title: Keep the Dropbox panel polling until the account link completes
head: 38c0ba78ab9d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A zero-exit, no-URL `dropbox-cli start` is not evidence that a browser link exists
leads.consequence: The shipped CLI's start() prints 'The Dropbox daemon is not installed!' and returns without error when its daemon binary is missing; it can also print 'Dropbox is already running!' when it cannot get a link URL. Both exit zero and contain no URL. The new branch erases lastError and actionStatus, shows 'Finish linking in your browser' and refuses subsequent Login clicks for five minutes even when no link page opened. On timeout it calls the situation 'Dropbox never confirmed the link', then allows a fresh attempt with the same result. Distinguish a known active link/daemon start from a merely zero-exit CLI call, and preserve/display diagnostic CLI output.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published as finding 2 (suggestion narrowed to 'not installed' per self-check F-D; H01's 'already running' case not treated as failure)

leads.summary: Check whether fast `status` polling revokes the very link URL the user is completing
leads.consequence: Every three-second tick launches status.py, which invokes dropbox-cli status even before linking. The shipped CLI's status() calls grab_link_url_if_necessary(), which issues needs_link to the daemon. The separate open #12988 claims each such call rotates cli_link_nonce and invalidates the open browser page. If this holds for client 268.4.4124, the new rapid polling repeatedly revokes the URL, so the account never links and the new timer reports failure after five minutes. The CLI's public source proves the repeated needs_link call but the proprietary daemon's nonce semantics need an isolated reproducer or a source/trace from the tested client. #12988's proposed guard omits status calls while unlinked; its test addition currently conflicts with this PR's test tail.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; attribution verified (#12637 issue reports mechanism, #12988 PR fixes it); published as hedged finding 1

leads.summary: New poll waits on sync folder existence, not just account-link completion
leads.consequence: For an info.json account block whose path does not yet exist, authenticated is false on every poll, despite any completed browser link. linkWait therefore times out after five minutes, with a false 'never confirmed' error even if the first sync creates the directory later. #8499 explicitly proposes treating the info.json account block as linked before the folder exists, but the exact write ordering of the proprietary daemon is not established in public source. Confirm with a synthetic info.json and an isolated version-matched Dropbox trace; do not infer that 3-second polls alone detect completion before the path is created.
leads.triage: unconfirmed daemon behaviour and pre-existing status.py semantics; dropped

leads.summary: Reconcile #8499's missing-URL retry with this five-minute wait before merging both
leads.consequence: The open #8499 starts loginRetry on every click, consults statusText for a URL, and reports 'Dropbox offered no login link' after 30 seconds. This PR starts linkWait for a no-URL success and deliberately waits five minutes for an out-of-band browser page. Their Service.qml edits produce four conflicting hunks using #8499's own base; merely keeping both timers would also surface a 30-second error while the user is still in the five-minute pending state. Coordinate the no-URL URL-discovery condition, error and completion timers, and test outcomes rather than selecting either side of each conflict independently.
leads.triage: already noted in PR description and Opus report; not published

leads.summary: The new QML test targets the wrong message if open PR #13412 merges
leads.consequence: #13412's own diff inserts a plain-text sync-status Text immediately before the action/error Text. Its diff applies to this head without rejects and both PRs are non-stacked. The fixture's unanchored `panel.replace(...)` then gives testStatusMessage to the first, sync-status Text. At fixture step 5 it compares that element's text to 'Unrelated control failure'; after applyStatus(linked:true) it is 'Up to date', so the runtime test fails on otherwise compatible production code (or would silently test the wrong node if assertion changed). Separately, #8400 moves the status message to a different indentation; resolving its textual conflict by retaining the moved error row likewise makes the first old-indentation match the 'No synced files found' row. Anchor injection to the actionStatus expression or expose a stable objectName. No Wayland runtime test was run without a reservation.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3; verified by coordinator (sol/merged-13412 Panel.qml:292 vs 303, #13412 open at 182948b5); published as optional test note

leads.summary: Combining #12988 needs manual test-file merge despite independent production changes
leads.consequence: #12988's test appends the unlinked-status regression immediately after the same Node heredoc that this PR follows with compositor gating. Applying #12988's diff to this head rejects that test hunk, and three-way merge from its own base produces a test-file conflict even though its status.py production fix can simply replace the unchanged helper. Preserve both tests and order the CLI guard assertion before require_compositor, or headless runs will skip the guard entirely. Both PRs are diverged and GitHub marks #12988 mergeable individually, which does not resolve their mutual test-file conflict.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus; mentioned in finding 1 suggestion

leads.summary: The runtime fixture does not test status.py actually detecting link completion
leads.consequence: The mock status.py always outputs authenticated:false; after waiting for two real Process exits, the fixture calls applyStatus(test.status(true)) by hand instead of changing the mocked account status and awaiting a third real poll. A plausible broken implementation, status.py permanently returns false (or rejects a newly written info.json), still passes all runtime assertions and falsely claims to cover late link detection. Add an evolving synthetic info.json/status.py response and assert the next statusProcess exit ends linkPending; keep the direct applyStatus case as a separate unit scenario. With no compositor, the shell test exits 0 before this fixture, so no QML assertion was executed in the sandbox run.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N2; published in optional test note

leads.summary: Fixture masks an incorrect production polling interval and timeout duration
leads.consequence: The fixture overwrites linkWait.interval to 50 ms before starting a login, and sets ticks directly to 99 plus manually emits triggered() for timeout. A plausible change from 3000 to 30000 in Service.qml still passes every runtime assertion, but would poll only once per 30 seconds and expire after fifty minutes rather than the advertised three seconds/five minutes. Assert the production interval before accelerating the fixture, and either test the tick count against the interval or factor the deadline into a testable property.
leads.triage: verified from fixture source (shell.qml sets interval 50 before assertions), confirmed in Opus self-check; published in optional test note

limits: No desktop or nested Wayland compositor was reserved. The review.py LC_ALL=C runs tested Node model assertions and QML text-format scanner only, not the runtime QML fixture.
The proprietary Dropbox daemon 268.4.4124 does not have publicly inspectable nonce creation or info.json write-order code; H02 and H03 are explicitly hypotheses, not verified daemon behavior.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** after a Login click, with or without a captured link URL, the service polls status every 3 seconds and stops as soon as `authenticated` is true, instead of waiting for the 60-second refresh. Pending clicks never run another `dropbox-cli start` and never reset the 5-minute deadline. The timeout message is kept in `linkError`, survives unlinked polls and clears on retry or late success, without touching unrelated `actionStatus` errors. The new Quickshell fixture exercises the real `Service.qml` and `Panel.qml`, fails on the base code, and caught 10 of 11 targeted mutations. The PR merges cleanly onto current `quattro` and the fixture passes there.

Two behaviours are worth a look: the faster poll multiplies calls that an open issue reports rotate the link nonce, and the no-URL wait also starts after a failed start.

### The 3-second poll multiplies calls that #12637 reports rotate the link nonce

Each `linkWait` tick calls `refresh()`, which runs `status.py`, which always runs `dropbox-cli status`. In the `dropbox-cli` source (nautilus-dropbox 2024.04.17 and current upstream), `status` calls `needs_link` whenever the daemon answers its command socket. Open issue #12637 reports that each such call mints a new `cli_link_nonce` and invalidates the previous one: the browser shows success, but the device never links.

Base already runs `dropbox-cli status` about 1 second after `start` exits (`delayedRefresh`), then on the 60-second refresh. During the link wait, head runs it every 3 seconds for up to 5 minutes: about 100 calls where base makes about 6. With a fake CLI that answers like the daemon in #12637 (synthetic, no real daemon or account):

```text
         dropbox-cli calls, seconds from shell start (Login click at 1.48)
base     start 1.48   status 2.51   (then the 60 s refresh, per source)
head     start 1.48   status 2.51, 4.51, 7.51, 10.51, 13.51, ...
```

A second click on head reopened the URL captured from `start`, although the fake daemon had issued two newer nonces by then (five by the end of the 14-second run). `login()` always reuses `_loginUrl`.

**Impact:** repeated rotation while the user is still in the browser is a plausible way for linking to fail on daemons that answer the socket, and "Click to reopen the Dropbox page" reopens the URL from `start`. The exact effect is unknown: the reporter of #12637 says raising the refresh interval to 3600 seconds worked around it, although that code also makes the 1-second call, so the reported model is incomplete. The daemon's nonce behaviour was not verified here. The client measured in the PR description did not answer its socket, so `status` never reached `needs_link` there. #10940 reports the same client version (268.4.4124) producing a `cli_link_nonce` URL during login and `dropbox-cli status` reporting that it is waiting to be linked, so a daemon that answers does occur with this version.

**Suggested change:** coordinate with open #12988, which skips `dropbox-cli status` while `status.py` sees no linked account (no account path in `info.json`, or that path is missing). The two PRs conflict only where both append to `test/shell.d/dropbox-test.sh`. Alternatively, make every unlinked status poll read only `info.json`, as #12988 does, so the nonce stays stable while the user is in the browser.

### A failed `dropbox-cli start` also enters the 5-minute wait

`loginProcess.onExited` treats exit 0 without a URL as "the daemon is up and has opened the link page itself" and calls `beginLinkWait()`. In the `dropbox-cli` 2024.04.17 source, `start()` returns nothing on every path, so the command exits 0 even after printing "The Dropbox daemon is not installed!" (also printed when no daemon PID appears within 60 seconds).

With a fake `dropbox-cli` whose `start` prints that failure and exits 0, and whose `status` prints "Dropbox isn't running!" (read by the real `status.py`; synthetic):

```text
         click 1                      click 2 (6 s later)
base     start runs, prompt remains   start runs again (retry)
head     linkPending = true           no start runs; the row stays in
                                      the waiting state (per Panel.qml)
```

**Impact:** after a start that failed, the Login row stays locked for 5 minutes and the failure text is not shown. The header controls are hidden while unauthenticated, so the only ways to run another start are the `p` (Resume) key or a shell reload, and the Login row itself stays waiting until the timeout or authentication.

**Suggested change:** do not enter the no-URL wait when the start output contains "The Dropbox daemon is not installed!", or let a pending no-URL click fall through to a fresh start after a shorter grace period. Broader string matches are risky: a healthy cold start can print "Dropbox isn't running!" before "Done!". `running` from `status.py` is not a reliable dead-daemon signal either: `status.py` stops `dropbox-cli status` after 4 seconds, so an alive daemon that does not answer also reads as not running.

**Optional test improvement:** the fixture adds `id: testStatusMessage` to the first `Text` block that matches its pattern in `Panel.qml`. Open #13412 inserts a sync-status `Text` with the same leading lines above the status message, so after it lands the id would attach to the wrong element and the fixture's status-message assertions would then fail. Giving the status `Text` a real `id` in `Panel.qml` avoids this. Separately, the fixture's status helper always reports unlinked and it sets the `linkWait` interval to 50 ms before asserting anything, so neither the poll-to-`finishLink()` chain through a real status process nor the production 3-second interval is covered.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `38c0ba78` against its base and current `quattro` (`3faafba2`), related open PRs and issues, and the public `dropbox-cli` source. The PR's fixture, 11 mutants and four scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox with Quickshell 0.3.1 offscreen, with the layer-shell keyboard panel stubbed. Apart from the fixture's own test hooks and the deliberate mutants, `Service.qml` and the tested `Panel.qml` bindings were unmodified. No compositor, real popup window, Dropbox daemon, account or browser was used. The live timing in the PR description was not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
